title: Renascor entry
description: A single catalogue entry describing a digital edition project of Renaissance-era written documents.

title.description: Name of the edition project or collection.

url.description: URL where the edition can be found. Must be a valid, resolvable URL.

doi.description: Verified DOI of the collection, edition or archived text dataset release, without the https://doi.org/ prefix. Do not use a grant DOI or a DOI for a related article or poster.

data_url.description: URL where the edition's machine-readable files can be obtained: a repository, a download page or a dataset record (e.g. GitHub, Zenodo, Oxford Text Archive). Give it whenever TEI or other XML files are publicly available. Optional; requires data_format.

data_format.description: Format of the files available at data_url, with the same vocabulary as encoding. Required when data_url is given.

languages.description: Languages of the texts, as human-readable names (e.g. 'Latin', 'Old French', 'Middle English').

encoding.description: Primary publicly available text format, using the richest published text data rather than internal encoding or the catalogue harvest format (TEI > other XML > JSON > HTML > wiki markup > plain text > Markdown).

status.description: active = online and maintained; archived = still online but no longer maintained; discontinued = no longer online (the URL may point to an archived copy).

provenance.description: How the entry was added. 'submitted' = contributed by a human via issue or pull request. 'discovered' = found by the automated weekly search.

date_added.description: Date the entry was added to the catalogue, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

author.description: Author of the source document(s), if known and applicable. Optional.

date.description: Date or period of the source document(s), e.g. '1492', 'c. 1470-1485', '16th century'. Optional.

institution.description: Institution, project team, or individual responsible for the edition. Optional.

words.description: Size of the resource text in words within 1450–1700, before content deduplication. Document source and coverage; harvested counts can cover only a subset. Omit if unknown.

texts.description: Number of resource text instances within 1450–1700, before content deduplication. Not a unique-work count. Document source and coverage; omit if unknown.

region.description: Geographic area covered by the corpus, e.g. 'Italy', 'Low Countries', 'Iberian Peninsula'. Optional.

countries.description: Present-day countries where the documents were written or printed, most important first: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, or ISO 3166-2 codes for the nations of Great Britain (GB-ENG, GB-SCT, GB-WLS, GB-NIR). Every code must be listed in schema/countries.json, which also groups the countries into the historical areas used by the public site.

period.description: Period covered by the corpus, e.g. '1450-1550', '16th century', 'Renaissance'. Optional.

years_active.description: Years during which the project was active. Optional.

end.description: Year the project ended, or the string 'ongoing' if still active.

notes.description: Additional information: scope, quality notes, access conditions, licence. Optional.

last_modified.description: Date of the last modification of the resource as reported by its host (GitHub repo last push, Zenodo record update). Optional; host-dependent.

license.description: Licence of the edition text, preferably an SPDX identifier or expression (e.g. CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0). Use Copyright, Custom terms, Mixed, Public domain or Not stated when appropriate. This is separate from the catalogue metadata licence.

license_url.description: Publisher page, dataset record or licence file supporting the edition-text licence.

license_note.description: Scope of the licence or differences between texts, annotation, images and other layers.

corpus_statistics.description: Renascor Corpus frozen in-core counts after the corpus duplicate filter. Kept separate from the catalogue resource size.

count_basis.description: Historical rq values count all retained in-core Renascor Corpus rows, including duplicates, with optional locked staging recovery. Sefaria counts individual Hebrew source versions of works composed within 1450–1700, excluding generated merged files and translations. See resource_statistics for the source audit.

resource_statistics.description: Source, retrieval date and method for a separate resource census. Takes precedence over the Renascor Corpus harvested-subset size while preserving corpus_statistics.

data_formats.description: All available download formats. Include data_format, the primary format. Optional; requires data_url.

api_url.description: Official documentation for programmatic access to the edition texts.
